subject: SSO tenant handoff failing — ambiguous IdP mapping for Acme Tools onboarding
messages:
From: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acmetools.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: onboarding@acmetools.com
Date: Sun, 25 Aug 2029 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Can't complete supplier portal binding — sees two possible SSO providers

Hi Markus,

We're almost finished with vendor setup but the portal is rejecting our "accept invite" step and shows an IdP mismatch. Our security team says Acme uses two IdPs (org-acme.onelogin.com and adfs.acme.local) depending on region/partner routing. When users click the activation link, they get a brief SAML redirect flash and then the page returns "tenant could not be resolved".

We've tried clearing cookies and hitting the link from different networks. A few users managed to accept when using incognito on mobile, but most still hit the error. Any chance you can bind our Ariba/Zip onboarding tenant manually or tell us what field in the SAML assertion the portal is matching on?

Happy to provide captures — attaching a sample SAML response from one of our failed attempts.

Thanks,
Alice Zhao
Onboarding Manager
Acme Tools

Attachments: idp-saml-response.txt (text/plain)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acmetools.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Aug 2029 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Can't complete supplier portal binding — sees two possible SSO providers

Hi Alice — thanks for the sample.

Quick notes from the platform side: Redwood's tenant resolution for supplier invitations prefers the SAML NameID in the format we expect (email or federated identifier) but we also perform an alias lookup against known tenant aliases. In cases where customers have multiple IdPs and inconsistent NameIDs, the resolution can flip between tenant aliases and result in the "could not be resolved" error you described.

Ben, can you take a quick look at Alice's SAML capture and the trace and advise whether a manual tenant bind is the safest short-term fix? If so, we should scope it to a specific org/tenant ID for Ariba and Zip so we don't create a broad override.

Alice — if you can share one failing request trace (HAR) and confirm which IdP the user selected in the flow, we'll triage.

I can schedule a 30-min window tomorrow afternoon for a manual handoff if needed.

— Markus
Director, Account Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acmetools.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Aug 2029 10:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Can't complete supplier portal binding — sees two possible SSO providers

Hey all,

Thanks for the details, Alice. I dug into the SAML response you attached — the assertion is valid, but the NameID format alternates between an email (alice.zhao@acme.com) and a persistent opaque ID (urn:acme:uid:12345) depending on which IdP handled the login. Redwood's automatic resolution checks NameID first, then tenant metadata (alias list). Because both IdPs map to separate aliases, some sessions match tenant-A while others map to tenant-B, which causes the linking to fail during the one-time invite flow.

Proposed short-term remediation:
- We can create a scoped manual tenant bind for the invite token so clicks during the maintenance window are forced to tenant-A (Ariba) or tenant-B (Zip) depending on the invite. This is reversible and won't affect other traffic.
- Alternatively, Alice's IdP team can add a transient attribute (e.g., acme:partner_tenant=ariba) in the SAML assertion to remove ambiguity — longer-term best practice.

I've attached the HAR from a failing session (sso-trace-20290825.har) and a minimal procedure for the manual bind. If you want us to do the manual bind, tell us which invite tokens (or user email addresses) to scope and the preferred window.

— Ben
Onboarding Operations Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sso-trace-20290825.har (application/http-archive)

From: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acmetools.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: onboarding@acmetools.com
Date: Wed, 28 Aug 2029 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Can't complete supplier portal binding — sees two possible SSO providers

Thanks Ben — that explanation makes sense.

We'll go with the manual tenant bind for the short-term to avoid blocking our procurement timeline. Please scope the change to the five invites we just sent to procurement@acme.com, procurement+east@acme.com, vendor-ops@acme.com, sally.kim@acme.com, and javier.mendez@acme.com and bind them to the Ariba tenant (tenant-A).

Preferred window: Thursday 29 Aug between 2:00–3:00pm EDT. Our IdP folks will be on standby in case you need live traces.

Also planning the longer-term fix with our IdP team to add acme:partner_tenant as an assertion attribute — I can follow up with a timeline.

Best,
Alice

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@acmetools.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Aug 2029 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Can't complete supplier portal binding — sees two possible SSO providers

Hi Alice — we performed the manual tenant bind for the five invite tokens at 14:10 EDT and then validated acceptance flows for two test users. All five invites were accepted successfully; logs show the redirect path now consistently resolving to Ariba tenant-A.

Ben: please mark ONB-7192 as "short-term bind applied; monitor 72h" and follow up with the platform team to add a softer detection rule so we reduce manual binds in future.

Alice — glad that unblocked your procurement work. Once your IdP team has a timeline for the assertion attribute change, loop Laura and Soojin in and we'll plan a coordination runbook for a permanent fix.

Closing the loop here — reopen if anything else pops up.

Thanks,
Markus
Director, Account Onboarding
Redwood Inference
